The watch\'s microphone takes short readings of the sound level around you. It keeps only the numbers (decibels). Audio is never recorded, stored or sent.
Levels are A-weighted (dBA), like the ear hears: very low and very high frequencies count less.
Level alerts use a 3-minute average, so a single bang never triggers one.
85 dBA for 8 hours is 100% of the day. Every 3 dB more halves the time: 88 dBA for 4 hours, 94 dBA for 1 hour.
The 7-day limit follows WHO-ITU H.870: 80 dB for 40 hours a week (75 dB for sensitive listeners). It rolls: old exposure drops off day by day.

Headphone levels are estimated from the volume and the type of output (±10 dB); the microphone never listens to them. Each minute counts once: headphones or surroundings, whichever is louder at the ear.
Watch microphones are not sound level meters: expect ±3–5 dB after calibration, more without. Treat every number as an estimate.
Only numbers are stored, and they travel only between your own watch and phone. Cloud AI is optional and off by default; it sees rounded totals only.

resources.string:
Your Voxara watch can include headphone listening from this phone in its weekly limit. This is optional and off until you turn it on.

What is sent to your watch whenever something changes (headphones connected or removed, play or pause, the volume moved): the time, how long, the media volume, and the type of output (wired, Bluetooth…). The watch turns this into an estimated level. While this is on, a small notification shows that Voxara is watching for headphones.

Never sent or stored: audio, song or video titles, app names, headphone names or Bluetooth addresses. Nothing goes to the internet; it travels only to your own watch.
